Owner class approval of 2026-10-29 (TypeScript type-level checks, verified for this row): the only case asserts with expectTypeOf that AgentTool params, execute() and prepareArguments() are typed by a TypeBox-shaped schema. Go mechanism: agent.AgentTool takes JSON arguments (json.RawMessage) that RunToolCall validates against the tool's schema (ai.ValidateToolArguments) after PrepareArguments, so Execute only runs with arguments of the schema's shape; there is no generic parameter type to assert. Go test: TestAgentToolArgumentsOfASchemaReachExecuteAsTheSchemaShape uses the upstream schema (required string command, optional "fast" | "deep" mode), decodes what Execute receives into that shape for a full call, an optional-less call, and refuses a bad mode, a missing command and a non-string command without executing; TestPrepareArguments_PreparedArgumentsAreStillValidated covers the prepared arguments.

Both upstream cases (:8 candidates[0] from the installed TUI package with the bundled-module fallback; :26 standalone-binary fallbacks when the package is unavailable) test getNativeModuleCandidates (packages/tui/src/native-module-path.ts:14-31), whose only caller is native-platform.ts:38: a Node require/dlopen search over prebuilt .node files (native/<os>/prebuilds/...). The shipped Node extension bridge runs that lookup through the vendored runtime-node/shims/pi-dist/pi-tui/native-module-path.js (imported by native-platform.js). No non-test Go resolves prebuilds/, win32-platform, pi-tui or native-module-path candidates. That Go-host absence is owner-approved design-out mechanics (CGO_ENABLED=0 native access); it does not remove the shipped Node bridge obligation, so the file is ported and its evidence stays verified.
